description: Sequential switch sending one input to whichever of sixteen outputs is currently selected, stepping forwards, backwards, at random or by an addressing voltage

params.text: Sets how many of the sixteen outputs are stepped through, from 1 to 16
Picks forward, pendulum, reverse, random or voltage addressed stepping, shown by the coloured lamps
In voltage addressed stepping, picks which output is selected, read at each clock edge; with a cable in the address CV input it attenuates that voltage instead
Chooses what an output does between its turns: S&H holds the value sampled when it was selected, the arrow returns it to 0V, T&H holds the last value that passed through

inputs.text: A high gate lets the switch step on and a low gate holds it where it is, stepping resuming at the next clock; with nothing patched here the switch always runs
Each rising edge moves the selection on by one step; any signal crossing 2V counts as a high gate
A rising edge sends the selection back to step one on the next clock, and until that clock arrives every output is held at 0V
Sets how many of the sixteen outputs are stepped through, 10V giving all sixteen, and takes the LENGTH knob out of circuit
Sets the stepping pattern by voltage and takes the DIRECTION knob out of circuit: under 1V forward, 1V to 2V pendulum, 2V to 3V reverse, 3V to 4V random, 4V and over voltage addressed
In voltage addressed stepping this voltage picks the output, 0-10V covering the whole set length whatever it is, with the ADDR knob attenuating it
The signal routed to the selected output; all channels of a polyphonic cable are carried through

outputs.text: Carries the input signal while that step is the selected one, and behaves between times as MODE is set

inputs.0: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.2: high above 2V · stepped · one channel only
